heading: 3. Nautilus, Great Northern Paper Mill, Millinocket — 60 MW Canceled Project
brief: Nautilus Data Technologies had planned a 60 MW data center at the former Great Northern Paper industrial site in Millinocket , with an initial investment proposal around $300 million . Announced in 2021, the development was originally expected to open by the end of 2022 and drew attention for its potential reuse of hydropower-adjacent paper-mill infrastructure. name: Sentinel / JGT2, Androscoggin Mill, Jay
heading: 2. Sentinel / JGT2, Androscoggin Mill, Jay — 82 MW Existing Utility Allotment; Project on Hold
brief: At the former Androscoggin Mill in Jay, Franklin County , property owner JGT2 Redevelopment and intended data-center operator Sentinel Data Centers had proposed converting industrial buildings into a roughly $550 million computing campus. The mill already held a Central Maine Power agreement for 82 MW of electric service. In an May 4, 2026 developer interview , JGT2 principal Tony McDonald said the data center might initially use around 50–55 MW and could grow toward the 82 MW utility allotment.

A February 2024 developer presentation delivered to the City of Glenarden cited up to 820 MW of overall site capacity. Unlike the two larger proposals, this facility is operating. WBUR reported September 11, 2026 that MGHPCC is permitted to draw up to 12 MW from the electricity grid and was using less than its maximum allowance. heading: 2. Chestnut River Power, Holyoke — 20 MW Proposed; Stalled
brief: A separate 20 MW data center proposal at 100 Water Street by Chestnut River Power and Infrastructure prompted debate about new AI computing facilities in Holyoke. On June 16, 2026 , the City Council voted 9–4 for a zoning restriction on new AI data centers above 12 MW, exempting the existing MGHPCC. name: Servistar Data Center Campus, Westfield
heading: 1. Servistar Data Center Campus, Westfield — 274 MW Proposed; Permit Extension Denied
brief: Servistar Realties proposed a 10-building campus across more than 150 acres in Westfield. The development’s reported 274 MW full-buildout electricity demand would have made it one of New England’s largest single data center plans. The Boston Globe reported that power requirement in September. It was not an energized facility: Servistar had not purchased the site land, and its initial 2021 permit remained unexercised.

In a September 17, 2026 company announcement , Hyperscale Data described roughly 340 MW of total potential campus capacity . Panattoni Development is preparing the industrial-zoned site for Google. The master plan includes three data-processing buildings along with supporting administrative and network-service structures. heading: 3. PowerCompute, Columbus — 11 MW Under Signed Utility Contract

heading: 2. Compass Datacenters, Meridian — 500 MW Original Supply Plan; 320 MW Current Campus Design

The project was introduced as a roughly $10 billion investment, including future tenants’ hardware, with an approximately eight-year buildout. The components are 536 MW of proposed grid supply and 500 MW of behind-the-meter baseload generation . heading: 3. CRG Festus — 600 MW Proposed After Major Redesign
brief: St. Louis-based CRG , a Clayco subsidiary, has scaled down its planned data center outside Festus, Jefferson County , from an initial 1,000 MW concept to roughly 600 MW . The company’s current official project page specifies four single-story data center buildings on about 173 acres of development area, while preserving an estimated 188 acres of woodland . heading: 2. Google Project Mica, Kansas City — Nearly 700 MW Under Development

Port KC’s official development record describes a nearly 500-acre , five-building campus with approximately 1.56 million square feet of data center space. name: Nebius Independence AI Factory
heading: 1. Nebius Independence AI Factory — Up to 1,200 MW Across Planned Power Sources
brief: Nebius is building a roughly 400-acre AI factory near Route 78 and Little Blue Parkway in Independence , east of Kansas City. Its March 3, 2026 announcement followed City Council approval of a Chapter 100 industrial development incentive plan and specified an eventual 1.2 GW campus . On May 12 , the company held a groundbreaking, independently confirmed by the Missouri Department of Economic Development . The first phase is under construction, but the whole 1.2 GW project is not online.

name: Hyperscale Data, BNI Montana
heading: 3. Hyperscale Data, BNI Montana — 125 MW Additional Power Under Conditional Utility Letter
brief: Hyperscale Data says it has a path to potentially add 125 MW at one of two leased Montana mining sites. In its June 24, 2026 company announcement , subsidiary BNI Montana reported receiving a formal conditional “will serve” letter from Lower Yellowstone Rural Electric Cooperative after a load study. The affected facility operates at approximately 10 MW supporting Bitcoin mining, the company said. name: Atlas Power, Butte
heading: 2. Atlas Power, Butte — 150 MW Expansion Proposal; 75 MW Existing Operating Site
brief: Atlas Power Group runs one of Montana’s better-established large data centers outside Butte, Silver Bow County . The Montana Department of Environmental Quality’s 2026 data-center information sheet lists the Butte facility at 75 MW of existing operating electricity load. The site primarily supports cryptocurrency mining rather than an announced large AI training installation.

name: Quantica Big Sky Campus, Broadview
heading: 1. Quantica Big Sky Campus, Broadview — 1,100 MW Proposed; Site Work Advancing
brief: Quantica Infrastructure , through its Big Sky Digital Infrastructure subsidiary, is planning a 1,100 MW data center and integrated power campus across approximately 5,100 acres near Broadview in Yellowstone County . The developer confirmed that scale in its August 31 announcement . The site is roughly 30 miles north of Billings. name: Monolith and Crusoe, Hallam
heading: 3. Monolith and Crusoe, Hallam — 35 MW Approved
brief: Monolith and Crusoe won approval on October 5, 2026 for a 35-megawatt modular data center on approximately ten acres at Monolith’s existing Olive Creek industrial campus in Hallam, Lancaster County . The Hallam Village Board approved the special-use permit unanimously after months of public meetings, according to Nebraska Public Media . The approval authorizes a planned facility, not an operating 35 MW IT load.

name: MARA Minden
heading: 2. MARA Minden — 42 MW Existing Grid-Connected Site
brief: MARA Holdings acquired a 42 MW nameplate-capacity data center in central Nebraska in January 2026 , expanding its operating mining infrastructure. MARA’s current portfolio identifies the facility as Minden, Nebraska , on approximately seven acres . Its first-quarter SEC filing distinguishes 35 MW of operating Bitcoin-mining capacity from the site’s 42 MW nameplate . The higher number is the installed facility’s rated capacity, not evidence of continuous 42 MW consumption.

name: MARA and Starwood Project Horizon, Kearney
heading: 1. MARA and Starwood Project Horizon, Kearney — Up to 368 MW Planned
brief: MARA and Starwood Digital Ventures are working on Project Horizon , a multistage data center redevelopment at Kearney’s Tech oNE Crossing business park. The official project website describes a 100 MW first phase using electricity already available to the adjacent Bitcoin mining operation. MARA’s corporate site gives 368 MW as the location’s longer-term gross potential, subject to expansion.
